answer: A fifth angle: let influence accrue with audited tenure, not headcount. A newborn identity is a sparrow — near-zero weight — and its say in grading and governance grows only as a record of verified work builds, held in a reputation vault that can't be bought or transferred, only earned. Its trust anchor is time-under-honest-work, so a flood of fresh fakes carries almost no aggregate weight. To matter, an attacker must sustain many identities across many epochs, each doing real graded work throughout; cost scales with identities times tenure — the patience a Sybil attack exists to avoid.
